title: Rigidity of perfect derived bialgebras with exterior residue cohomology
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring: every ideal is finitely generated, $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal, and $k=R/\mathfrak m$. In the cochain derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the signed total derived tensor product $\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}$, let $K$ be perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Suppose there are morphisms $u:R[0]\to K$, $\mu:K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\to K$, $\varepsilon:K\to R[0]$ and $\Delta:K\to K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$. They make $K$ a commutative bialgebra object: $\mu$ is associative, unital with unit $u$, and invariant under tensor symmetry; $\Delta$ is coassociative with counit $\varepsilon$; $\Delta$ and $\varepsilon$ preserve multiplication and units. All these equalities are in $D(R)$ under its canonical tensor associativity, unit and symmetry isomorphisms. Let $\overline K=k\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$. Assume $H^*(\overline K)$ with the induced product is the exterior algebra on the finite-dimensional vector space $H^1(\overline K)$, with its generators in degree one, and $H^0(\overline K)=k$ via $u$. Put $g=\dim_kH^1(\overline K)$. Then $K$ is isomorphic in $D(R)$ to a bounded complex of finite free $R$-modules with zero differentials, zero outside degrees $0,\ldots,g$. The map $H^0(u)$ identifies $H^0(K)$ with $R$, and $H^1(K)$ is free of rank $g$. Every $x\in H^1(K)$ has $x^2=0$, and multiplication induces an isomorphism of graded $R$-algebras $\bigwedge_R^*H^1(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^*(K)$ [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra].

source.place: Agent-stated bialgebra rigidity lemma; minimal-model input is Tag 0BCC (lemma-lift-pseudo-coherent-from-residue-field); separatedness of the maximal-ideal filtration is algebra.tex Tag 00IP (lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero). Neither tag alone states the rigidity conclusion.

proof.text: Choose a bounded cochain complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules representing $K$, using [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] to each of its finitely many nonzero terms $M$ at the prime $\mathfrak m$: there is $f\notin\mathfrak m$ with $M_f\cong R_f^{\oplus r}$. Since $R$ is local, $f$ is a unit, so $R\to R_f$ and $M\to M_f$ are isomorphisms and $M\cong R^{\oplus r}$ is finite free. Thus this is a bounded finite-free representative, in particular a bounded-above one, so $K$ is pseudo-coherent by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Tag 00NX, lemma-finite-projective (finite projective modules are locally free); apply at the maximal ideal of the local ring to the terms of the perfect representative.

proof.text: Put $d_i=\dim_k H^i(\overline K)$. The exterior-basis statement [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis] gives $d_i=\binom gi$ for $0\leq i\leq g$ and zero otherwise. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-local-pseudocoherent-free-model]: there is a representative $P$ of $K$ with $P^i=R^{d_i}$ in every degree. It is therefore bounded and supported in $[0,g]$. It is minimal: for the residue complex $E=k\otimes_R P$, the equality $\dim_k E^i=\dim_k H^i(E)=d_i$ and the formula $\dim H^i(E)=\dim E^i-\operatorname{rank}(\overline d^{i-1})-\operatorname{rank}(\overline d^i)$ force all residue differentials to vanish. Hence $d(P)\subseteq\mathfrak mP$.

source.place: Tag 0BCC, lemma-lift-pseudo-coherent-from-residue-field; exterior dimensions from algebra.tex Tag 00DM.

proof.text: The bounded free complexes $R[0]$, $P$ and all finite tensor powers of $P$ are K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]; freeness makes tensoring termwise a finite direct sum, hence exact. By [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] their ordinary signed total tensors compute the derived tensors. Use [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] to represent $u,\mu,\varepsilon,\Delta$ by chain maps on these complexes. The same bijectivity says that each bialgebra identity holds up to chain homotopy, since its source is bounded projective. On reducing modulo $\mathfrak m$, all terms $dh+hd$ vanish. Thus $E$ is a strict graded bialgebra with underlying graded algebra $H^*(\overline K)$ and with the given exterior product.

source.place: Tag 064K, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism; morphism representatives are derived.tex Tag 064B, lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex.

proof.text: The residue of $u^0:R\to P^0$ is an isomorphism by the hypothesis on $H^0(\overline K)$. Apply [lem-pc-finite-free-map-residue-localization] at $\mathfrak m$. Its $f\notin\mathfrak m$ is a unit, so $u^0$ itself is an isomorphism. Identify $P^0$ with $R$ by this map. The chain-map equation $d^0u^0=0$ gives $d^0=0$. In particular the unit is an actual cycle, and its leading differential in every maximal-ideal order is zero.

source.place: Tag 00O0, lemma-cokernel-flat (3); the local-ring specialization uses that every element outside the maximal ideal is a unit.

proof.text: Write $V=E^1$. Since $E$ has no negative degrees, $E^0=k$ via the unit, and the counit is zero in positive degrees, its two counit equations imply $\overline\Delta(v)=v\otimes1+1\otimes v$ for $v\in V$. Multiplicativity of $\overline\Delta$, with the signed tensor product, gives the $(1,1)$-component $c(vw)=v\otimes w-w\otimes v$. Choose a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_g$ of $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis], the $e_ie_j$ with $i<j$ form a basis of $E^2$. Define $\rho:V\otimes_kV\to E^2$ by $\rho(e_i\otimes e_j)=e_ie_j$ for $i<j$ and zero for $i\geq j$. Then $\rho c=1$. Consequently $c$ is split injective and every primitive element of $E^2$ is zero. This includes characteristic two, and $E^2=0$ when $g<2$.

source.place: Agent coordinate calculation from the exterior basis in Tag 00DM, section-tensor-algebra; no assertion about primitive elements is attributed to Stacks.

proof.text: We prove by induction on $n\geq1$ that every entry of $d$ lies in $\mathfrak m^n$; step 2 is the base case. Suppose this holds for $n$, and put $I_n=\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. The differential induces a degree-one $k$-linear map $\delta:E^i\to I_n\otimes_k E^{i+1}$: for $a\in P^i$, take $da$ in $\mathfrak m^nP^{i+1}/\mathfrak m^{n+1}P^{i+1}$ and use the identification with $I_n\otimes_k E^{i+1}$ given by a free basis of $P^{i+1}$. Changing $a$ by an element of $\mathfrak mP^i$ changes $da$ by an element of $\mathfrak m^{n+1}P^{i+1}$, proving independence of the lift. Step 4 gives $\delta(1)=0$.

source.place: Agent maximal-ideal filtration calculation on the finite-free model from Tag 0BCC; this calculation is not the statement of a Stacks lemma.

proof.text: The chain-map equations for the chosen representatives are $d\mu=\mu(d\otimes1+(-1)^{\deg}1\otimes d)$ and $\Delta d=(d\otimes1+(-1)^{\deg}1\otimes d)\Delta$. Take their coefficients in $\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. Every occurrence of $d$ contributes its leading coefficient $\delta$; every adjacent coefficient of $\mu$ or $\Delta$ can be reduced modulo $\mathfrak m$, since its error times $\mathfrak m^n$ lies in $\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. We obtain $\delta(ab)=\delta(a)b+(-1)^{\deg a}a\delta(b)$ and $\overline\Delta\delta=(\delta\otimes1+(-1)^{\deg}1\otimes\delta)\overline\Delta$, with the coefficient factor $I_n$ placed first on both sides. These are identities of $k$-linear maps with values in $I_n$ tensored with the indicated graded modules.

source.place: Agent coefficient calculation using the chain-map equations on the Tag 0BCC model; only the equations, not strictification of all bialgebra laws, are used.

proof.text: For $v\in E^1$, substitute $\overline\Delta(v)=v\otimes1+1\otimes v$ and $\delta(1)=0$ into the second equation of step 7. It says $\overline\Delta(\delta v)=\delta v\otimes1+1\otimes\delta v$. Its $(1,1)$-component is $(1_{I_n}\otimes c)(\delta v)=0$. Tensor the explicit retraction $\rho$ of step 5 with $I_n$ to conclude $\delta v=0$; no flatness of $I_n$ is needed. The first equation of step 7 now gives $\delta(v_1\cdots v_r)=0$ by induction on $r$, since $E$ is generated by $E^1$ and the unit. Thus $\delta=0$, so every entry of $d$ lies in $\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. This completes the induction for all $n$.

source.place: Agent derivation and reduced-coproduct calculation, extending the minimal-model input Tag 0BCC; the split retraction was explicitly constructed in step 5.

proof.text: Every matrix entry of $d$ belongs to $N=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\mathfrak m^nR$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-localization] with the Noetherian ring $R$, ideal $\mathfrak m$, finite module $R$, and prime $\mathfrak m$. It gives $f\notin\mathfrak m$ with $N_f=0$. Because $f$ is a unit, this says $N=0$ already over $R$. Therefore $d=0$. We have proved the asserted derived isomorphism to a bounded finite-free zero-differential complex supported in $[0,g]$, without completing $R$.

source.place: Tag 00IQ, lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module (1), specialized to the maximal ideal of a local ring; compare Tag 00IP, lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero.

proof.text: Put $A^i=P^i=H^i(K)$. All tensor powers of $P$ now have zero differential. Consequently every chain homotopy between their maps has boundary $dh+hd=0$, so the bialgebra laws from step 3 hold as exact graded-module identities on $A$. By step 4, $A^0=R$ via $H^0(u)$; by step 2, $A^1$ is free of rank $g$. The counit equations, degree by degree, imply $\Delta(x)=x\otimes1+1\otimes x$ for every $x\in A^1$, just as in step 5.

source.place: Agent passage from the zero-differential finite-free model to its cohomology; the homotopy representatives were justified by derived.tex Tag 064B in step 3.

proof.text: Let $c_R:A^2\to A^1\otimes_R A^1$ be the $(1,1)$-component of $\Delta$. Its residue is the split injection $c$ of step 5. Both source and target are finite free, so [lem-pc-finite-free-map-residue-localization] and the fact that $R$ is local make $c_R$ injective. For $x\in A^1$, multiplicativity and the signed tensor product give $\Delta(x^2)=(x\otimes1+1\otimes x)^2=x^2\otimes1+x\otimes x-x\otimes x+1\otimes x^2$. Hence $c_R(x^2)=0$, so $x^2=0$. This is the required square-zero assertion, even when $2$ is not a unit.

source.place: Tag 00O0, lemma-cokernel-flat (1); the signed square calculation is elementary and uses no division by 2.

proof.text: Associativity, signed commutativity and step 11 make $(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\mapsto x_1\cdots x_r$ multilinear and alternating: move two equal factors next to one another using the signs, then their square is zero. By [lem-trf-exterior-power-universal-property] it induces $\phi_r:\bigwedge_R^r A^1\to A^r$ with the stated value on pure wedges. The source is finite free by [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis]; the target is finite free by step 2. Its residue is the exterior-product isomorphism in the hypothesis: exterior basis vectors reduce to the corresponding exterior basis vectors over $k$, and the product maps reduce to the given product. Apply [lem-pc-finite-free-map-residue-localization] at $\mathfrak m$ to obtain that each $\phi_r$ is an isomorphism. Both sides vanish for $r>g$ (and negative degrees); for $r=0$ the map is $H^0(u)$. On pure wedges concatenation and associativity give $\phi_{r+s}(\alpha\wedge\beta)=\phi_r(\alpha)\phi_s(\beta)$, so the direct sum of the $\phi_r$ is the required graded-algebra isomorphism.
